subject: BYOK scope & operator telemetry — EU export control considerations
messages:
From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@novamedical.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: oleg@thirdparty-audit.com
Date: 2026-10-07T08:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deploy terms — BYOK + telemetry questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Legal and Security here at NovaMedical have two items they want clarified before we proceed with a private VPC deployment:

1) BYOK controls: we need explicit contract language that clarifies that customer CMKs remain under our control, and that Redwood will not have access to plaintext keys or the ability to export them. Is there an operator break-glass process that still preserves cryptographic separation?

2) Operator telemetry: our compliance team is ok with minimal operational telemetry for troubleshooting, but they require confirmation that telemetry does not include model inputs/outputs or PII. Any proposal here should list telemetry fields and retention windows.

Also, NovaLegal asked about cross-border export controls — if we store keys in an EU HSM but place some operator services in another region during failover, what contractual guarantees can Redwood provide to prevent key egress?

I attached the DPA redline from our counsel. Oleg (cc) is available to review telemetry samples if needed.

Next steps: can you share a short note (with proposed contract language bullets) we can present to legal by EOD Friday?

Best,
Maria
Director, IT Risk — NovaMedical

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@novamedical.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-07T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deploy terms — BYOK + telemetry questions

Maria — thanks, and great questions. High level answers below; I'll follow with proposed DPA/Annex language and a telemetry field list.

1) BYOK custody: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) via customer KMS/Cloud HSM or customer-premised key material. In private deployment we operate with a cryptographic handshake: the runtime holds only wrapped key material and uses a local KMS plugin for unwrap/sign. Redwood operators do not receive plaintext keys as a matter of design. We can add contract language that explicitly states "Redwood personnel shall not have access to plaintext customer CMKs" and require HSM attestations on provisioning.

2) Operator break-glass: we support a documented, auditable break-glass. Any emergency operator action that could access key material requires a council of two customer-approved admins + recorded session + ephemeral justification token. We can commit to preserving cryptographic separation by requiring unwrap operations to occur only inside customer-managed HSMs under a dual-control flow.

3) Telemetry & retention: Redwood can provide a telemetry manifest (fields and retention). By default, operational logs include: host/service health, scheduling events, GPU metrics, error traces (stack/exception), and anonymized request offsets for performance debugging. We exclude prompt text, model outputs, and raw request payloads from operator-facing telemetry. Retention can be set to a 30-day default for hosted support traces, with options to reduce to 7 days for strict deployments. We will provide a sample telemetry CSV for review.

4) Cross-border failover: we can implement a regional lock for key unwrap so that key material never leaves the EU HSM; any failover that would require cross-region unwrap will use a fallback model variant that is stateless. Contractually, we can add a clause: "Customer CMKs shall not be exported from the designated region (EU) except under a mutually approved emergency process documented in the Annex." We also recommend geo-fencing operator nodes and explicit subprocessor restrictions.

I'll work with Priya on explicit DPA/Annex language and Neha on telemetry manifest. Expect a draft by EOD Thursday.

— Karthik
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Maria — following Karthik, attaching a concise telemetry manifest for your security team. Quick highlights:

- Operator-facing telemetry fields (examples): node_id, pod_id, container_health, cpu/gpu_util_pct, memory_usage_mb, inference_latency_ms_aggregate, batch_size, error_code, orchestration_event_id.
- Explicitly excluded fields: request_text, completion_text, embeddings_payload, any header/body PII.
- Retention plan: default 30 days; can be configured to 7 days with legal EP clause. All telemetry is hashed/anonymized at collection point; session IDs are one-way hashed.

Regarding the DPA redlines: Priya and I propose an Annex A (Private Deployment Security) that includes: subprocessor list limited to named infra partners; a customer-approved subprocessors addendum workflow; and an HSM attestation requirement upon initial provisioning.

If Oleg wants to validate the manifest against his audit playbook, happy to schedule a short call.

Neha
Product Security Manager, Redwood Inference

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@novamedical.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-07T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deploy terms — BYOK + telemetry questions

Maria — adding proposed contract bullets for your legal team. These are intended as redline-ready language snippets you can drop into the DPA/Annex: 

1) Customer CMK custody: "Customer shall provision and retain sole control of Customer Master Keys (CMKs). Redwood shall only process wrapped key material and shall not access, export, or persist plaintext CMKs. All unwrap operations shall occur within Customer-managed HSMs or a customer-designated KMS under the control of Customer."

2) Operator break-glass and emergency access: "In rare emergency scenarios, Redwood personnel may initiate an emergency access request that requires: (a) authorization from two designated Customer security contacts; (b) real-time recorded session; and (c) a post-action forensic report. Emergency access will be scoped to narrow troubleshooting tasks and will not permit extraction of plaintext CMKs."

3) Subprocessor and geo-restriction obligations: "Redwood will provide a list of subprocessors limited to named infrastructure partners. Any proposed addition of a subprocessor that would process keys or telemetry will require Customer written consent. Key material and key unwrap operations shall not be exported outside the EU without Customer pre-approval; any emergency exception will follow the documented emergency process above."

4) Telemetry: "Operational telemetry provided to Redwood personnel shall be limited to the manifest attached as Annex B; telemetry shall exclude request/response payloads and shall be retained for no longer than the retention period selected by Customer (default 30 days)."

We can also add an SLA item that Redwood will provide attestation evidence (HSM config, hardware certs) during onboarding and annually.

If these look reasonable I'll prepare a redline of the DPA and a short Annex to attach to the CDM.

— Priya
Head of Compliance Programs, Redwood Inference

Karthik/Neha/Priya — appreciate the detailed responses and the language snippets. Legal reviewed Priya's bullets and we have two small asks before we sign:

1) Add an explicit statement that Redwood will not run any model updates or training on customer data or in environments where customer CMKs are used, unless mutually agreed and under a separate SOW.

2) For the emergency exception that allows cross-region unwrap: require an independent third-party attestation post-event (within 5 business days) confirming no plaintext keys were exported and a forensic timeline.

If Redwood agrees to those two additions we can accept the Annex and move to signatures. Oleg: if you want to join a 30-minute call tomorrow for a quick run through the attachments, we're available 09:00–11:00 CET.

Thanks — Maria
